Package com.wgblackmon.aihealthcare.infrastructure.ingestion.feed

Record Class FeedSourceConfig

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.wgblackmon.aihealthcare.infrastructure.ingestion.feed.FeedSourceConfig
Record Components:
topicId - FK to Topic.id — scopes this feed to a newsletter topic.
name - Human-readable label used in logs, metrics, and sourceName on articles.
topic - Grouping label stamped on every harvested article's topic field. Multiple feeds can share the same topic so articles appear under one section header on the news listing page. Falls back to name when null or blank.
url - Fully-qualified RSS, Atom, or web page URL.
tier - Harvest tier controlling scheduling and scoring weight.
baseWeight - Baseline relevance multiplier applied before AI scoring (0.0 – 1.0; higher = more trusted source).
maxItems - Maximum number of items to ingest per harvest cycle (RSS/Atom only).
keywords - Optional keyword filter for COMPETITOR-tier web pages. Empty = no filter.
public record FeedSourceConfig(Long topicId, String name, String topic, String url, FeedSourceConfig.FeedTier tier, double baseWeight, int maxItems, List<String> keywords) extends Record
Immutable configuration descriptor for a single RSS/Atom feed source.

Encapsulates all metadata needed by RomeFeedHarvester to fetch, identify, and tier-weight articles from a given feed URL. Instances are constructed from FeedSourceProperties at application startup and held in a List injected into the harvester.

The topicId field scopes this feed to a specific newsletter Topic. During harvest, it is propagated to every NewsArticle produced from this feed so that articles, vector embeddings, and newsletter output can all be filtered by topic without infrastructure changes.

The tier field drives scheduling and relevance-score weighting:

  • ACADEMIC – daily harvest, higher base relevance weight
  • REGULATORY – event-driven / daily, very high signal value
  • INDUSTRY – frequent harvest (every few hours), needs AI filtering

The optional keywords list applies only to COMPETITOR-tier sources processed by WebPageHarvester. When non-empty, a page change is only emitted as an article if at least one keyword appears (case-insensitive) in the extracted page content. An empty list disables filtering (all changes are accepted).
